observations.detail: The complete title reads 'The relation between simple harmonic motion and circular motion' in three clean lines. The English chapter/page breadcrumb wraps without collision. All 17 normalized prose paragraphs remain readable from the opening radius-vector explanation through the closing experiment explanation, with clear spacing, no first-line indentation and no text crossing the 16px page margins. The 17 count agrees with the report and saved HTML paragraph tags; it is not the source prose-block count.

Visible mathematics includes omega with subscript zero, the OA vector arrow, O with subscript one followed by X, t = 0, the absolute-value/vector amplitude relation, phi = omega-zero times t, and the full x = x_m cos(phi) = x_m cos(omega-zero times t) relation. Vector arrows, subscripts, phi, omega, equality signs and absolute-value bars are resolved and readable. The cosine relation fits the mobile line. No raw TeX delimiters, missing-glyph boxes or formula/prose collisions are visible. This assesses rendering, not the already-approved science.

Two horizontal rules are actually visible, not merely inferred from section_breaks metadata. The first separates 'The ball itself continues around the circle; it does not move back and forth along that axis.' from 'We can make this projection visible as a shadow.' The second starts the spring-comparison section at 'Hang a weight from a spring where the same parallel light can reach it.' Its preceding section ends with the projection-versus-ball explanation, followed by Figure 10 and its caption before the rule. Saved HTML contains exactly two para section elements with border-top styling; these are paragraph borders, not standalone hr elements.

The full sentence 'The spring weight and the shadow of the uniformly rotating ball follow the same displacement law.' is visibly bold on three lines, separate from the surrounding normal-weight paragraphs. It is complete, readable and not clipped; the saved HTML retains strong markup around the conclusion.

Each numbered caption is visible once, centered below its corresponding diagram and clear of nearby prose or separator rules. The bound lesson's source caption blocks contain only the figure identifiers. No descriptive caption is required or invented; English apparatus labels within diagrams are not additional captions.

The dashed circular path, center, radius/vector arrows, angle arc, rotation arrow, vertical projection axis, projected point and dashed guides are distinguishable. A, O, O-subscript-one, X, x, x-subscript-m, phi and omega-subscript-zero are all readable. Arrowheads and subscripts are present; labels do not collide with one another or leave the image. The circle and full axis are contained.

Parallel light arrows, rotating disk, ball, center/radius, shadow point, slanted screen outline, vertical axis and displacement arrow remain clear. Light, Ball, Shadow, Disk, Screen, A, O, O-subscript-one, X and x are readable. Leader lines identify their objects without hiding text. The right-side screen and O-subscript-one fit inside the image; no apparatus or label is clipped.

The spring/support and weight, disk/ball, light arrows, projected weight and ball, upper filled and lower outline positions, dashed guides, displacement arrows and equilibrium leader are individually visible. Spring, both Weight labels, Shadows, Ball, Light, x-subscript-m, Disk, Screen and Equilibrium are readable. The dense shadow region retains space between labels and objects; Equilibrium and Screen fit below their respective apparatus. Intended guide-line/apparatus intersections do not obscure labels. No missing glyph, label overlap or canvas-edge clipping is visible.

Despite its definitionScreenshot field and polarization filename, this image shows a scrolled introductory viewport containing Figure 9 and the first paragraph, not a separate definition or the conclusion. The title's first line intersects the top capture edge because of the saved scroll position. The full-page screenshot shows the entire title with top margin, so this is a capture-boundary limitation, not evidence of page-layout clipping. Conclusion and separator approval comes from the full-page pixels.

summary: PASS for the five bound saved mobile images: readable English and formulas, 17 normalized paragraphs, two visible section rules, a complete bold conclusion, source-only numbered captions and three legible 358px diagrams. No actionable clipping, overlap or missing-glyph defect observed.
